title: Sales Enablement: Prospect Enterprise Pack — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
summary: A single-page prospect-facing pack for enterprise sellers that consolidates core positioning and messaging, short competitive brief, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance and examples, two compact case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospective customers.
content:
Overview

This document is a curated prospect pack for enterprise sellers engaging with technical and security-conscious buyers. It is intended for demo-to-close conversations and should be used in conjunction with the full Enterprise Playbook. Use the messaging and security FAQ during discovery and the pitch deck outline and pricing guidance during commercial discussions.

1) Core positioning & messaging

- Target audience: platform/infra engineering teams, ML engineers, and product teams at mid-market and enterprise companies.
- One-liner: Redwood Inference — predictable, cost-efficient, production-grade LLM inference with unified tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Key value props (short):
  - Production-first performance: GPU-optimized runtime with latency SLOs and autoscaling for predictable throughput.
  - Cost controls & optimization: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations to reduce per-token cost.
  - Deployment flexibility: hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC / on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations.
  - Observability & guardrails: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, model-level dashboards, and quality/regression alerts.

- Messaging play (technical buyer): emphasize runtime architecture (continuous batching, KV cache, optimized kernels) and ability to pin model versions + rollout policies. Include recent benchmark figures when available.
- Messaging play (product/biz buyer): emphasize predictable economics, SLA-backed Dedicated options, and security/compliance for regulated workloads.

2) Short competitive brief (1 page)

- Competitors to call out: major cloud AI endpoints, LLM API providers, and inference orchestration vendors.
- Typical competitive differentiation table (talking points):
  - Feature: Deployment modes — Redwood: Hosted / Dedicated / Private; Cloud managed endpoints: Hosted + some private; Self-hosted runtimes: Private only.
  - Feature: Production telemetry — Redwood: token-level cost/latency, rollouts, tracing; Competitor A: limited telemetry; Competitor B: basic metrics only.
  - Feature: Cost controls — Redwood: automated batching/caching suggestions and quantization profiles; Competitor A: manual tuning.
  - Feature: SLA & enterprise support — Redwood: SLA for Dedicated + enterprise support; Competitor C: SLA on limited plans.

- How to win: lead with a small technical POC on a representative workload, measure latency/cost vs current stack, and highlight rollback/rollout safety for model upgrades.

3) Pitch deck — 10-slide outline (seller notes)

Slide 1: Title — Customer name + one-line value statement.
Slide 2: Executive summary — 3 bullets: performance, cost, compliance.
Slide 3: Market context — why inference engineering matters for product velocity and cost.
Slide 4: Redwood value props — visual: runtime + routing + deployment abstraction.
Slide 5: Deployment options & decision matrix — hosted vs dedicated vs private (one-liner recommended uses).
Slide 6: Performance benchmarks & expected economics — representative numbers for latency and token cost (replace with project-specific benchmark).
Slide 7: Security & compliance controls — KMS, audit logging, VPC, SOC/ISO status.
Slide 8: Case studies — 2 short examples (see below).
Slide 9: Pricing & commercial proposal — recommend starting point and negotiation levers (see pricing guidance).
Slide 10: Next steps & POC plan — timeline, success criteria, owner names.

Tips for presenters: keep slides data-driven, include a small demo or live cost comparison if the prospect is technical, and always close with a defined POC success criteria: target throughput, 95th percentile latency SLO, and cost per 1M tokens.

4) Pricing guidance & examples

Pricing model summary:
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation + per-embedding unit) with free credits for evaluation.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual) for predictable throughput; overage and burst pricing available.
- Private: licensing + support (one-time platform fee + annual support), typically for regulated customers.

Commercial levers for negotiation:
- Commitment term: 12 vs 36 months (longer terms unlock deeper discounts).
- Committed throughput: baseline reserved GPU-hours or tokens; discounts scale with committed capacity.
- Data residency & retention: add-on for retention beyond default window.
- Observability retention and advanced SLAs: premium add-ons.

Example proposals (templates for AE to adapt):
- Small Enterprise POC: 3-month pilot, Dedicated small pool (4 A100-equivalent GPUs), up to 50M tokens/month, $X/month credit applied to usage, outcome-based success criteria.
- Mid-tier adoption: 12-month reserved capacity (16 GPUs), 15% discount vs list, 6-month ramp, included onboarding workshop.
- Regulated (Private): one-time platform license $Y + annual support 18% of license, includes KMS/HSM integration and SOC2 evidence handoff.

Guidance: always document the expected per-token economics for the prospect's canonical workload (use our cost calculator; link in related pages). When in doubt, propose a small POC with observable success metrics.

5) Two compact case studies (seller-ready)

Case study A — FinTech analytics vendor (mid-market)
- Problem: inconsistent latency and unpredictable token cost when scaling chat features to 3 product teams.
- Solution: migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV caching and workload-aware batching, and configured model rollouts for safety.
- Outcome: 60% reduction in per-token cost, stabilized 95th percentile latency to 180ms, and zero production regressions during two model upgrades.
- References: internal contact: Sarah Jansen (solutions engineering), demo artifacts linked in related pages.

Case study B — Healthcare enterprise (regulated)
- Problem: required on-prem inference with strict data residency and audit logging.
- Solution: Private deployment with VPC-controlled control plane, HSM-backed key management, and extended audit log retention.
- Outcome: achieved compliance with customer's internal audit, completed go-live in 10 weeks, and met SLA of 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (Top 10)

Q1: Do you offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment?
A1: Yes. We provide a Private option with a customer-managed control plane, and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments.

Q2: How do you handle encryption and key management?
A2: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+. Data at rest can be encrypted; for Private deployments customers can integrate with KMS/HSM (BYOK).

Q3: What audit logging and traceability do you provide?
A3: Token-level request logs, model versioning traces, and admin audit logs. Additional log retention and SIEM integration are available as an add-on.

Q4: Can Redwood meet our compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO)?
A4: We maintain SOC2 Type II and provide ISO evidence packages. For regulated customers we support compliance-driven deployment patterns and assist with attestations.

Q5: How do you isolate customer data in Dedicated?
A5: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with network and storage isolation. We also offer per-tenant encryption keys and restricted access controls.

Q6: How are third-party model artifacts vetted?
A6: We maintain a curated model catalog with verified performance profiles and vetting checks; customers may onboard custom models through the model-onboarding process.

Q7: What is your incident response process for security incidents?
A7: We follow the company incident response process with an on-call rotation, triage runbooks, and post-incident reviews. For private deployments we provide an agreed-upon SLA and notification process.

Q8: Can we restrict model access and function calling?
A8: Yes — Redwood supports role-based access controls (RBAC), per-route policies, and the ability to constrain function/tool calling at the API surface.

Q9: How long do you retain request data, and can retention be adjusted?
A9: Default request retention is 30 days for hosted plans; retention windows can be extended for enterprise customers as an add-on. Private deployments follow customer retention policies.

Q10: What security reviews do you support during procurement?
A10: We provide a security questionnaire, artifact package (SOC2/ISO certificates), architecture diagrams, and a technical contact for security deep-dives.

7) Sales playbook & objection handling (quick reference)

- Objection: "We can just use cloud provider endpoints cheaper."
  - Response: run a short POC comparing latency and per-token cost on representative workload; emphasize observability and production features that reduce ops burden and regression risk.
- Objection: "We can't move data off-prem."
  - Response: propose Private deployment with KMS/HSM integration and on-prem packaging; provide the case study for a similar customer.
- Objection: "We need predictable pricing."
  - Response: propose Dedicated reserved capacity with SLA and predictable per-unit economics plus commitment discounts.

8) Operational & enablement checklist (for AE + SE)

- Before POC: collect canonical workload (sample prompts, average sequence length), expected peak RPS, latency targets (p50/p95), and security/compliance constraints.
- POC plan: 2-6 week plan with setup steps, success criteria (throughput, p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens), and rollback plan.
- Post-POC: operations handoff to customer success, add monitoring dashboards and alerting for model regressions.
